drills.q: Logging bill is $30k/month. First three moves?
drills.a: 1) Volume-by-log-name report to find offenders. 2) Exclusion filters on _Default for health checks + system info logs (often 40-60% cut). 3) Tier retention: compliance copies to GCS/BQ instead of extended bucket retention; keep queryable windows only. Then budget alerts at 50/80%.

drills.q: Can you shorten _Default retention? What happens to expired logs?
drills.a: Yes, project-level buckets configure 1-3650 days. Shortening: expired logs become unqueryable but a 7-day grace period lets you restore access by extending again; grace-period logs still bill.

drills.q: Design alerting for a checkout API at 99.9% availability SLO.
drills.a: Availability SLI from request counts (exclude health checks); multi-window burn alerts: page at 1h>=14.4x AND 5m>=14.4x, ticket at 6h>=6x AND 30m>=6x; wire to on-call with runbook links; document budget policy (freeze threshold) before go-live.

drills.q: SLO dashboard green for months but users complain daily. Diagnose.
drills.a: SLI likely measures wrong plane or averages away recurring pain: health-endpoint uptime vs real flows; server-side latency missing client time; weekly window hiding daily storms. Fix: client-perspective synthetics, per-endpoint SLIs, segment slicing by region/tenant/version.

drills.q: Spans vanish between service A and B through an internal LB. Likely causes?
drills.a: LB/proxy stripping traceparent headers; instrumentation version mismatch; sampler dropping parent while keeping children. Verify header propagation hop-by-hop, align OTel versions, embed context into message payloads at async boundaries.

drills.q: Team wants everything queryable for 2 years in Log Explorer. Cost-aware counter-proposal?
drills.a: Hot bucket 30-90d for incident windows; aggregate/compliance copies routed to GCS or BQ-linked Log Analytics for long-term - not extended bucket retention ($0.01/GiB/mo compounding). Query needs beyond that window are rare and served from cold tier.

drills.q: Budget alert fires at 80% mid-month. What automation should already exist?
drills.a: Pub/Sub-triggered actions from budget notifications: cap autoscaling ceilings, disable non-prod schedules, notify owning team with labeled attribution. Alerts without pre-wired responses are just early disappointment.

drills.q: Error budget exhausted; product lead refuses deploy freeze. What failed?
drills.a: Governance, not telemetry: the freeze must be executive-agreed when the SLO is signed, with documented escalation. An error-budget policy without teeth agreed upfront is dashboard decoration.

drills.q: Why do structured logs earn their payload overhead?
drills.a: Same $0.50/GiB ingestion buys filterable fields instead of regex archaeology: log-based metrics, precise sink routing, SQL analysis via Log Analytics, mechanical trace-ID correlation. Signal-per-GiB rises dramatically; enforce schemas via libraries+CI linting.

drills.q: Alerting pricing lands in 2027. Delete half the alert policies now?
drills.a: No - audit and consolidate dead/duplicate policies as hygiene, model post-pricing spend from policy counts, prefer log-based metrics where they collapse references. Deleting working coverage to dodge future pricing optimizes the wrong thing.
